messages:
alex: heads-up — starting regional staggered rollout for release v2.3.1 in the 22:00 UTC change window. plan: US -> EU -> APAC. pinning model=redwood-llm-v2.3.1, inference-runtime=1.14.0. keeping canary at 10% first slice.
maya: ack. pin noted. running preflight capacity checks now.
sam: tagging infra: @ops-scheduler please confirm warm pools for US/EU/APAC and any thermal constraints.
ops-scheduler: preflight results: US warm-pool healthy (12/15 GPUs ready), EU warm-pool borderline (6/8 ready, 2 initializing), APAC warm-pool low (3/10 ready). recommendation: proceed US -> EU but hold APAC until extra warm-up or reduce APAC canary to 2%.
maya: APAC low is expected during our maintenance window. can we do a soft-pin for APAC (route <=2% until warmup)?
alex: yes. plan update: US 10% -> hold 10m -> EU 10% -> hold 10m -> APAC 2% gated. rollback triggers: error-rate >1% sustained 5m OR p95 latency increase >300ms over baseline for 5m. anyone object?
eva: add request-failure-rate (4xx/5xx) and model-quality regression alert (eval set spike). if QA set fails >1% differences we stop.
sam: agree. also log-level dump if p50 crosses 200ms.
deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] starting canary slice: region=us, version=redwood-llm-v2.3.1, slice=canary, traffic=10% :rocket:
deploy-bot: canary preflight passed (healthchecks ok).
alex: kicking off smoke tests for US now. running ablation set and 5 short prompt tests.
maya: smoke tests green except one slow request from edge us-east-2 (p95=860ms). isolating instance now.
sam: pulled logs: OOM warnings on instance gpu-12-us-east. scaling group added 1 warm node, telemetry shows KV cache miss spike at cutover.
ops-scheduler: scaled, warm-up in progress. new node status: initializing -> ready (3m).
deploy-bot: canary slice us reached steady-state at 10% after 8m. metrics: error_rate=0.18%, p95=420ms, p50=95ms.
eva: quality evals pass on sampled prompts. no regressions.
alex: proceeding to EU canary. keeping an eye on cost gating.
deploy-bot: starting canary slice: region=eu, version=redwood-llm-v2.3.1, traffic=10%
maya: EU went to 10% — initial p95=380ms, error_rate=0.12%. warm pools still at 6/8 but draining fine.
sam: note — a routed partner test hit an unexpected tokenization error in a non-default tokenizer. submitting quick fix to model config but not pushing to prod. monitor only.
ops-scheduler: EU stable for 12m. no action.
alex: prepping APAC hold. @maya please coordinate whether we give additional warm-up or lower canary to 1% until midnight.
maya: recommend lower to 1% for immediate safety, trigger ramp to 5% only after warm-pool >=7/10 and p95 < 500ms for 10m.
deploy-bot: APAC canary request received: target=2% (as requested). attempt to allocate warm nodes... allocation failed: insufficient capacity in apac-region-a. error: "insufficient_gpus"
sam: looks like capacity constraint in apac-region-a; we have spare in apac-region-b (zone B) but cross-zone latency penalty ~30ms.
alex: decision: HOLD APAC rollout. keep US/EU in prod. set APAC route to fallback EU for now and open a change ticket to reschedule APAC ramp once warm-pool >=7.
eva: publishing release notes update: add note about APAC delayed ramp and fallback routing to EU. include rollback criteria and contact for on-call.
ops-scheduler: created incident-lite ticket #INC-8242 for APAC capacity shortfall, assigned to oncall infra. ETA for extra capacity: 90m.
deploy-bot: rolling back any partial APAC traffic assignments to EU fallback. routing rules updated.
alex: thanks everyone. follow-ups: (1) infra to confirm warm-pool increase in APAC, (2) release docs updated, (3) ops to monitor error-rate and p95 for next 30m. hold until ops says green before any APAC ramp.
maya: noted. I'll keep thread updates hourly or on state changes.
sam: will post logs if anything breaches triggers.
ops-scheduler: monitoring enabled. current global p95=410ms, global error_rate=0.17%. next status check in 15m.
deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] summary: US=canary->prod slice rolled, EU=canary->prod slice rolled, APAC=hold (fallback to EU).
